beats.line: My Gym Jarvis checked twenty-three sets, and called stop on a good one.
beats.visual: Wall of 23 sets fills the frame, then one tile flashes a red STOP stamp.

beats.line: So let's open my Workout Analyser.
beats.visual: Gym Jarvis zoom diagram: push in from the whole Gym Jarvis system to the Workout Analyser block.

beats.line: First, I had Claude go through over 200 papers and tools.
beats.visual: Research blocks stack up with a counter running to 200+.

beats.line: And I realized, counting reps is easy, but judging a rep is hard.
beats.visual: Research blocks sort into two piles: EASY (counting reps) and HARD (judging a rep).

beats.line: So I built one tool and two agents.
beats.visual: SEE -> JUDGE -> CHECK block diagram draws in, all three blocks visible.

beats.line: The pose tool tracks my joints, and rep maths turns each rep into a wave.
beats.visual: SEE block lights up; skeleton overlay on the footage, with one joint angle drawing out the rep wave.

beats.line: One wave is one rep, and its height is how far I moved.
beats.visual: Rep wave with one wave highlighted and a height arrow labelled 'how far I moved'.
Rep wave continues and the later waves visibly shrink.

beats.line: And against my best, rep four is clearly shorter.
beats.visual: Best-rep ghost line appears over the lat pulldown wave; rep 4 is called out as 62 vs 86.

beats.line: The first agent, the judge, reads my numbers.
beats.visual: JUDGE block lights up in the block diagram, with the rep numbers flowing into it.

beats.line: The second, the coach, isn't allowed the numbers.
beats.visual: CHECK block lights up as the coach; the numbers feed is crossed out and only video goes in.

beats.line: And if a joint is hidden, it refuses to judge.
Then I ran every set: six got continue, eleven got hold, and two got stop.
beats.visual: 23-bar results dashboard (taller = better): 6 continue, 11 hold, 2 stop, 4 can't see.

beats.line: Except this one, where the judge said stop and the coach said good.
beats.visual: Lunge set: judge STOP vs coach GOOD, side by side.

beats.line: I'd only turned towards the camera.
beats.visual: Lunge footage with skeleton overlay as I turn towards the camera; the research block with the camera-angle warning pops back in.

beats.line: So now, stop needs both agents, or I check the footage.
beats.visual: Both-agree gate: two keys make STOP, one key routes to CHECK FOOTAGE.

beats.line: And only one stop survived, my reverse crunch, which was fair.
beats.visual: Reverse crunch ghost line, 53 vs 122, then the dashboard settles on the final 1 stop, 1 check footage.

beats.line: Next up: Salesforce is reportedly letting people go, but hiring people with AI experience.
How can you be that one? Follow along to know.
